used_for: FIG_02 'The clock of shadows' (Making Of article CH_03, concept lunar-base): 5 s / 150-frame seamless loop of one lunar day of sunlight rotating around de Gerlache crater, with permanently shadowed regions highlighted.
publisher: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (LOLA GDR) + NASA GSFC PGDA (Barker et al. site products)
usage_terms: US Government work / public domain; attribution requested (NASA/GSFC/MIT LOLA; Barker et al.)
citation: Terrain: PGDA Site11 5 m/px de Gerlache-rim tile + site11_regional 20 m/px crop (Barker et al. 2021/2023 - see terrain-dems.json for hashes) inset in a hole-matched frame; shadow-casting skirt: LOLA GDR LDEM_75S_60M V2.0 crop (see fig01-south-pole-map.json entry, sha 7724861d...). Smith, D.E., et al. (2010), Space Sci. Rev. 150, 209-241.

entries.notes: Scene: 20 m regional terrain copy (subsurf render 3) + 5 m Site11 tile copy datum-aligned at z-30 (fills the inset hole in the regional mesh) + 60 m FIG_01-crop skirt as 4 bands tiling AROUND the regional footprint (no overlap; skirt extent = full FIG_01 coverage, 100-158 km of shadow casters in every direction incl. the Malapert massif). All terrain carries the standard flat-plane curvature correction z -= d^2/2R from the frame center (R 1737.4 km) - without it, distant peaks falsely occlude the grazing sun (validated: az-NE frame went from 0.3% to 25.9% lit). SUN CONVENTION (logged per spec): elevation 1.0 deg = the select_base_site.py sunlit threshold (horizon < 1.0 deg; real oscillation +-1.5 deg noted in that script); azimuth full 360 deg CCW (physically correct sense at the south pole viewed from above), 150 frames x 2.4 deg, frame 151 == frame 1 (verified pixel-identical, max delta 1/255) and dropped from the encode so frames 1-150 loop seamlessly. Camera: ortho top-down 65x65 km, x[-75,-10] y[-26.5,+38.5] km from the pole (Kari's marked crop, calibrated + approved 2026-07-26). Frame crop fully on 20 m data.

entries.source: PSR mask computed FROM THE ANIMATION'S OWN FRAMES (150-frame sweep)
entries.product: fig02_psr_sdf.png (signed distance field, 0.5 = boundary, 1 px = 47.238 m) + psr_mask_major/_full.png, packed in the blend
entries.notes: Operator: per-pixel MAXIMUM illumination staying at the indirect floor = never directly lit (the brief said 'minimum'; a min-composite marks ever-shadowed pixels instead - caught by its own sanity check at 98% PSR - same intent, corrected realization). Threshold at the histogram valley; de Gerlache PSR stable 381-396 km2 across thresholds 16-37. VALIDATION vs site-selection sun-sweep: base pixel lit 90/150 frames = 0.600 vs illum_frac_horizon_proxy_2m 0.562 (site11.layout.json); 6 cold traps within 3 km of the base (0.60 km2, nearest 566 m) matching the F_01 'small cold trap a few hundred meters away' copy. Major mask = components >= 0.05 km2. Note: mask reflects this model (1.0 deg fixed elevation, 65 km frame + 150 km skirt, no seasonal +-1.5 deg sweep) - an illustration-grade PSR, not a Mazarico-style survey product.
